deep.reconstruction:
The page holds four unrelated layers.

(A) Bibliographic notes, top, in pencil. These are references for the historical section of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Ueber die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe', written 1853 and submitted Dec. 1853.
(i) 'Schumacher, Astronomische Nachrichten Nr. 374, 16. Bd., 1839' with the title 'Ueber den Ausdruck einer Function φ(x) durch Cosinusse und Sinusse der Vielfachen von x'. This is Bessel's 1839 note on Fourier series, which Riemann cites in exactly this form ('Schumacher, Astronomische Nachrichten Nr. 374') in §3 of the Habilitation.
(ii) '... Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik, Bd. IV, S. 157'. This is Dirichlet's 1829 paper 'Sur la convergence des séries trigonométriques qui servent à représenter une fonction arbitraire entre des limites données' (Crelle 4, 157–169), the central reference of the Habilitation.

(B) Bernoulli genealogy, in pencil and in French. It serves the Habilitation's history of the vibrating-string controversy (Daniel Bernoulli, Euler, d'Alembert).
- At the head: Nicolas Bernoulli, member of the Grand Council of Basel, i.e. the father.
- Jacques (Jakob) Bernoulli, † 1705.
- Jean (Johann) Bernoulli, married 6 March 1694 to Dorothée Falckner (Falkner).
  - Born at Basel 27 July (Old Style) 1667.
  - Maître ès arts 1685; in Paris 1691–92; doctor of medicine 1694.
  - Professor at Groningen 28 Nov. 1695; professor of mathematics at Basel 17 Nov. 1705.
  - † 1 Jan. 1748, at seven in the evening.
- His three sons:
  - Nicolas (II): professor of law at Bern, called to the imperial academy at St Petersburg, † 1726.
  - Daniel: doctor of philosophy and medicine, professor of anatomy and botany.
  - Jean (Johann II): doctor of law and philosophy, professor of mathematics.
- These data agree with standard biographies.

(C) Draft of a short personal note in ink, heavily corrected, dated 'Göttingen, den 2. April 1853', signed 'B. Riemann'.
- Addressed 'Liebe Frau' or possibly 'Liebe Tante'.
- Content: at the addressee's request he asked Syndicus Wiederhold when the post to Dannenberg leaves. It leaves this afternoon; items must be handed in by 4 o'clock; the next opportunity is Wednesday.
- Dannenberg is the district town near Quickborn, where Riemann's family lived.
- The date fixes the bibliographic notes to the period of Habilitation work.

(D) Calculations, lower right, in ink. They appear to have been written with the sheet turned upside down, which explains the inverted-looking glyphs in the machine transcription. They are only partly legible.
- The visible structure is a sequence of rows of the form 0 = A·∂²ω/∂x² + B·∂²ω/∂x∂y + C·∂²ω/∂y² + (first-order terms). Some rows have side annotations to the right of a vertical rule defining auxiliary quantities, e.g. ratios such as x/y.
- A lower block contains rows with factors (x/y + 1) and (x/y − 1), alternating. This suggests the characteristic directions x = ±y of a wave-type (hyperbolic) operator.
- A separate isolated line at the bottom left gives a substitution of the form x/y = (σ+1)/(σ−1) (reading uncertain).
- Interpretation (mine, tentative): Riemann is transforming a linear second-order PDE in two variables under a change of variables built from the ratio x/y and the combinations x/y ± 1. This could reduce it to canonical or characteristic form, or to an ODE for solutions homogeneous of degree 0.
- Example (my illustration): for ω = f(t), t = x/y, one gets ω_xx − ω_yy = y^{-2}[(1 − t²) f'' − 2t f'].
- This fits the previous page, which contains ∂²ω/∂p∂q = ω-type equations and Jacobian inversion formulas for (u,v) ↔ (p,q). It also fits the next page, which works with z = (x + iy − a − ib)^α and differential relations of the form ∂z/∂p·(p − 2a) + z − z₁ = βz.
- The individual coefficients cannot be read reliably enough to reconstruct each row.
errors: No mathematical errors can be asserted, because the PDE rows are largely illegible.

Biographical data check out against standard sources: Johann I born 27 July (O.S.) 1667, married Dorothea Falkner 1694, Groningen 1695, Basel 1705, died 1 Jan 1748; Nicolaus II died 1726 in St Petersburg.

deep.surprise_reason: The bibliographic and Bernoulli notes are clearly working notes for the 1853/54 Habilitation, whose citations (Bessel AN 374, Dirichlet Crelle 4) are already known. The dated letter draft (2 April 1853) is a minor biographical datum. The PDE manipulations look like routine variable changes.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',positive=True); f=Function('f'); t=x/y; w=f(t); e=simplify(diff(w,x,2)-diff(w,y,2) - ((1-t**2)*f(t).diff(t,2) if False else 0)); print(simplify((diff(f(x/y),x,2)-diff(f(x/y),y,2))*y**2))
checkable.asserts: Illustrative (my interpretation): for ω = f(x/y), y²(ω_xx − ω_yy) equals (1 − t²) f''(t) − 2t f'(t) with t = x/y, showing why factors (x/y ± 1) appear.
The substitution x/y = (σ+1)/(σ−1) is an involution: σ = (r+1)/(r−1) when r = x/y.

transcription_corrections: Line 2 should read approximately 'Ueber den Ausdruck einer Function φ(x) durch Cosinusse und Sinusse der Vielfachen von x' (Bessel's title in AN Nr. 374); the dangling 'x.' is the end of this title.
Line 3: '[Crelle,] Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik, Bd. IV, S. 157' = Dirichlet 1829.
'Nicolas Bernoulli, membre du grand Conseil à Bâle' is the father of Jacques and Jean, written as the head of the tree.
Nicolas II line reads roughly 'professeur en droit à Berne, appelé [?] à l'ac. imp. de St Pétersbourg, † 1726'.
Salutation may be 'Liebe Tante' rather than 'Liebe Frau' (uncertain).
The mathematical block at lower right appears written upside down. The machine transcription's 'ɐ', '6', 'ɟ', 'ɯ' glyphs are inverted ∂, y, m etc., so its formulas are unreliable.
The bottom-left formula is probably x/y = (σ+1)/(σ−1) or similar, not '(…+1)/(…+1)'.
